clue.text: Plan to wander around Turkey's capital, say

indicators.note: around tells us the wandering word wraps the letters that follow

parts.note: to stray is to wander off course

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one, so Turkey's capital is its opening letter

parts.note: e.g., for example, is what 'say' introduces

explanation.surface: A travel plan: drift aimlessly around the Turkish capital, perhaps Ankara.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey's capital' tempts you towards Ankara; it is only the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is a plan of action devised to reach a goal.

clue.text: Work hard on an advertising catchphrase

indicators.note: on places the first word above the next in this down answer

parts.note: to slog is to toil, work hard

explanation.surface: Toiling away on a catchy line for an advert.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan is a memorable motto or phrase used in advertising.

clue.text: Rumour about fortified wine

parts.note: re means about, concerning
port is a wine fortified with brandy

explanation.surface: Gossip doing the rounds about some fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A report can be gossip or hearsay, as in 'by all reports'.

clue.text: Street cop, potentially restricted

indicators.note: potentially says these letters could become something else once rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer on the street whose movements might be limited.
explanation.definitionFit: Top secret is the highest classification of restricted information.

clue.text: European female departs holding lead of poodle, her dog

parts.note: a German is a European

indicators.note: holding means the earlier letters keep the later ones inside them

parts.note: she is a female pronoun
D is the abbreviation for departs, as on timetables

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A European woman leaves with her poodle on a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog leash in this surface; it simply means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The German shepherd, or Alsatian, is a large breed of dog.

clue.text: Petty Officer and wife, sensational success in meeting

parts.note: W stands for wife, as in genealogies
a wow is a huge hit, a sensational success

explanation.surface: A naval officer and his spouse score a great hit at some gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is an informal word for a conference or discussion, from a Native American gathering.

clue.text: Complete circuit, or small part

parts.note: a bit is a small part

explanation.surface: Choosing between a full lap or just a short section.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is one full revolution around a body, a complete circuit.

clue.text: Battle station

definitions.meaning: the 1815 battle where Napoleon was defeated

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a famous Belgian battle and a large London railway terminus named after it.

clue.text: Trouble hiding blemish? Just the opposite with cosmetics

indicators.note: hiding says one word is concealed inside another
just the opposite reverses the stated roles, so the blemish hides the trouble rather than the reverse

parts.note: a wart is a blemish on the skin
pain means trouble or bother

explanation.surface: Using make-up to cover a skin blemish, or rather the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the trouble would hide the blemish; 'Just the opposite' flips who does the hiding, so the blemish wraps the trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: War paint is a jocular term for women's make-up, from the face paint of warriors.

clue.text: On which one will study, in part, Royal St George's?

definitions.text: On which one will study, in part
definitions.meaning: a programme in which study alternates with periods of work experience
the famous championship golf links at a Kent town of the same name

explanation.surface: Wondering whether one might study at a celebrated golf club.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal St George's is the Open Championship golf course at Sandwich, a town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of study broken up by work placements, and literally a golf course at Sandwich.

clue.text: Operating daily, in theory

parts.note: a machine that is on is operating
a daily is a newspaper published every day, a paper

explanation.surface: Something running every day, in principle at least.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle but may fail in practice: an idiom for theoretically.

clue.text: Rarebit cooked for judge

indicators.note: cooked suggests the word rarebit is worked over and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Welsh rarebit prepared for a judge, perhaps in a cookery contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast, so 'cooked' sits naturally beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone who settles disputes, a referee or judge.

clue.text: A nearly new suit

indicators.note: nearly says the word for new loses its final letter

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced, as in a green recruit

explanation.surface: A suit of clothes that is almost brand new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' reads as a noun, but the answer is the verb: to suit is to agree with.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: if food does not suit you it does not agree with you; both mean be compatible.

clue.text: Check on old artist touring independent theatres

parts.note: to audit is to check accounts

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the artist's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An inspection of an elderly painter who tours as an independent performer around theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: Auditoria is a plural of auditorium, the part of a theatre or hall where the audience sits.

clue.text: Sauce on dress and robe

indicators.note: on places the first part before the second in this across answer

parts.note: a dressing is a sauce for salad
a gown is a dress

explanation.surface: Spilling sauce on your dress and robe at dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing gown is a loose robe worn over nightclothes.

clue.text: Upset at charges, attend uninvited

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: Annoyed at the price of entry, someone turns up without an invitation.
explanation.definitionFit: To gatecrash is to go to a party or event without being asked.

clue.text: Capone's type of joint — marvellous

definitions.note: read as 'Capone is', so the definition is the gangster himself

parts.note: a scarf is a joint in carpentry where two pieces are bevelled to overlap
ace means excellent, marvellous

explanation.surface: Praise for the kind of joint, drinking den perhaps, run by Al Capone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint' suggests a speakeasy; it is a woodworking joint.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chicago gangster Al Capone was nicknamed for the facial wound he carried.

clue.text: Jokes about boy heading for Roedean in best clothes

indicators.note: about says the jokes go around the next pieces

parts.note: gags are jokes
a lad is a boy

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Jokes about a boy heading for a girls' school, dressed in his finest.
explanation.walkthrough: Roedean is a well-known English girls' boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is an informal idiom for one's smartest clothes.

clue.text: Exercise control over what the photographer takes?

definitions.meaning: to be the one making decisions and giving orders
a photographer takes shots, so a literal reading: summon the pictures

explanation.surface: Wondering about the sort of control a photographer exercises over a shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be in charge and make the decisions, as a director does.

clue.text: I must get information on American virtuoso

parts.note: gen is slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone insisting they be briefed on an American virtuoso.
explanation.definitionFit: A genius is someone exceptionally gifted, a master of their art.

clue.text: Left one by a rich heiress

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single wealthy heiress was abandoned.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Merchant of Venice, Portia is the wealthy heiress of Belmont wooed by Bassanio.

clue.text: I'd a chicory mostly growing wild, an Italian variety?

indicators.note: growing wild suggests the letters run riot into a new order
mostly means the word chicory loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A plant grower's note on chicory running wild, perhaps an Italian strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims chicory to CHICOR; with I'D and A, 'growing wild' scrambles the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Radicchio is a red-leaved Italian variety of chicory, so the definition leans on the chicory in the clue.

clue.text: Talk about conclusion of bizarre con

indicators.note: about says the talk goes around the next letter

parts.note: to chat is to talk

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Discussing how a strange swindle ended.
explanation.definitionFit: To con is to swindle or deceive, the same as to cheat.

clue.text: Set of beliefs, note, held by Conservative party

indicators.note: held by says the note sits inside the following letters

parts.note: a do is a party
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A political party's manifesto, noted and adopted by the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo, Latin for 'I believe', is a creed or statement of principles.

clue.text: A strange team game, recalled layman

indicators.note: strange signals the word team is put into an odd order
recalled means called back, so the game's letters run backwards

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game

explanation.surface: An odd team, a game remembered, and a non-professional involved.
explanation.definitionFit: An amateur is a non-specialist, someone without professional expertise, like a layperson.

clue.text: Pragmatic type in Israel, wasted little time

indicators.note: wasted suggests the country's name is ruined and its letters rearranged

parts.note: T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A practical person in Israel who frittered away a small amount of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A realist is someone who sees things as they are and acts practically.

clue.text: Mock some keepers at zoo

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Taunting some of the zookeepers at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' looks like the verb to tease; here it is the adjective, meaning imitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes a substitute or imitation, as mock does in 'mock turtle soup'.

clue.text: Wager heads turned in chapel

parts.note: a bet is a wager

indicators.note: turned suggests the word heads is turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Betting on heads turning up at a church gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Bethesda is a common name for a Nonconformist chapel in Wales, after the biblical pool.
